children.content: General Requirements.
General Requirements.

A Marijuana Establishment is required to be registered to do business in the
Commonwealth as a domestic business corporation or another domestic business entity in
compliance with {{ref:500.000}} and to maintain the corporation or entity in good
standing with the Secretary of the Commonwealth, DOR, and DUA.

Control Limitations.
1. No Person or Entity Having Direct or Indirect Control shall be granted, or hold, more
than three licenses in a particular class, except as otherwise specified in {{ref:500.000}}.
2. An Independent Testing Laboratory or Standards Laboratory Licensee, or any
associated Person or Entity Having Direct or Indirect Control, may not have a License
in any other class.
3. To the extent that persons or entities seek to operate a testing facility in the Counties
of Dukes County and Nantucket, {{ref:500.200}} applies.
4. The Commission shall receive notice of any such interests as part of the application
pursuant to {{ref:500.101}}.
5. Licensees and Persons or Entities Having Direct or Indirect Control holding Licenses
that allow them to cultivate Marijuana are limited to a maximum Canopy of 100,000
square feet distributed across all applicable Licenses, inclusive of MTC Licenses.
6. Limitations on the Number and Control of Delivery Licenses.
a. No Third-party Technology Platform Provider shall be a Licensee, or a Person or
Entity with Direct or Indirect Control of a Delivery Licensee.
b. A contract between a Delivery Licensee and a Third-party Technology Platform
Provider shall be negotiated and entered into on an arm's length basis. A Delivery
Licensee may not accept any investment in the Delivery Licensee by a Third-party
Technology Platform Provider with which they have a contract.
c. No Person or Entity Having Direct or Indirect Control shall be granted or hold
more than a total of three Delivery Operator and three Marijuana Courier Licenses
at any time.
d. No Delivery Licensee may share its profits of the sale of Marijuana or Marijuana
Products with a Third-party Technology Platform Provider, or otherwise provide a
percentage or portion of the sale of Marijuana or Marijuana Products to the
Third-party Technology Platform Provider.
7. Limitations on the Number and Control of Microbusiness Licenses.
a. Cultivating Microbusiness Licensees shall have the Microbusiness license count
towards the total limit on Marijuana Cultivation licenses granted or held for any
Person or Entity Having Direct or Indirect Control.
b. Manufacturing Microbusiness Licensees shall have the Microbusiness license
count towards the total limit on Marijuana Product Manufacturing licenses granted
or held for any Person or Entity Having Direct or Indirect Control.
8. Limitations on the Number and Control of Craft Marijuana Cooperatives. A Craft
Marijuana Cooperative Licensee shall be limited to one license and a total of 100,000
square feet of Canopy; provided, however, that a Craft Marijuana Cooperative Licensee
may apply for additional Licenses in accordance with {{ref:500.050(3)(i)}}.
9. Limitations on the Number and Control of Social Consumption Establishments.
a. No Person or Entity Having Direct or Indirect Control shall be granted or hold
more than three Supplemental On-site Consumption licenses, three Hospitality
On-site Consumption licenses, and three Marijuana Event Organizer licenses.
b. A Hospitality On-site Consumption Licensee and a Marijuana Event Organizer
Licensee shall not:
i. Convey an ownership or control interest in the license as a condition of being
housed or hosted by a Non-Cannabis Entity; provided however, this provision
shall not apply where the Non-Cannabis Entity and a Hospitality On-site
Consumption Licensee or Marijuana Event Organizer Licensee share the same
Persons or Entities with Direct and Indirect Control.
ii. Provide a set percentage or a set portion of sales to the Non-Cannabis Entity.
A Hospitality On-site Consumption Licensee and a Marijuana Event Organizer
Licensee may pay a fee or rent to the Non-Cannabis Entity for housing or hosting
the Social Consumption Establishment; provided however, this provision shall
not apply where the Non-Cannabis Entity and a Hospitality On-site Consumption
Licensee or Marijuana Event Organizer Licensee share the same Persons or
Entities with Direct and Indirect Control.
Marijuana Cultivator (Indoor or Outdoor).
Marijuana Cultivator (Indoor or Outdoor).

A Marijuana Cultivator may cultivate, Process and package Marijuana, to transport
Marijuana to Marijuana Establishments and to Transfer Marijuana to other Marijuana
Establishments, but not to Consumers.

Tier Expansion. A Marijuana Cultivator may submit an application, in a time and
manner determined by the Commission, to change the tier in which it is classified. A
Marijuana Cultivator may change tiers to either expand or reduce production. If a Marijuana
Cultivator is applying to expand production, it shall demonstrate that while cultivating at the
top of its production tier, it has sold 85% of its product consistently over the six months
preceding the application for expanded production for an indoor cultivator, or during the
harvest season prior to the application for expanded production for an outdoor cultivator.

Tier Relegation. In connection with the license renewal process for Marijuana
Cultivators, the Commission will review the records of the Marijuana Cultivator during the
six months prior to the application for renewal for an indoor cultivator or during the harvest
season prior to the application for renewal for an outdoor cultivator. The Commission may

reduce the Licensee's maximum Canopy to a lower tier if the Licensee sold less than 70% of
what it produced during the six months prior to the application for renewal for an indoor
cultivator or during the harvest season prior to the application for renewal for an outdoor
cultivator.

An eligible Marijuana Cultivator may operate a Supplemental On-site Consumption
license within its existing Marijuana Establishment Premises.
Craft Marijuana Cooperative.
Craft Marijuana Cooperative.

A Craft Marijuana Cooperative may be organized as a limited liability company, limited
liability partnership, or a cooperative corporation under the laws of the Commonwealth.

The Members or shareholders of the cooperative shall be residents of the Commonwealth
for the 12 months immediately preceding the filing of an application for a license.

The Craft Marijuana Cooperative shall have:
1. One Member that has filed a Schedule F (Form 1040), Profit or Loss from Farming,
within the five years prior to application for licensure; or
2. An agreement to lease land wholly owned by a person or entity that has filed a
Schedule F (Form 1040), Profit or Loss from Farming, within the five years prior to
application for licensure.

Where the agreement to lease land in {{ref:500.050(3)(c)}}2. renders the individual
or entity filing a Schedule F (Form 1040) a Person or Entity Having Direct or Indirect
Control, the Craft Marijuana Cooperative shall report the individual or entity and submit the
agreement, as required by {{ref:500.101(1)(a)}}1.

The Craft Marijuana Cooperative shall operate consistently with the Seven Cooperative
Principles established by the International Cooperative Alliance in 1995.

The cooperative license authorizes it to cultivate, obtain, Manufacture, Process, package,
brand and Transfer Marijuana Products and to deliver Marijuana to Marijuana
Establishments, but not to Consumers.

The Craft Marijuana Cooperative is limited to one license, under which it may cultivate
Marijuana, subject to the limitations of {{ref:500.050}}. The cooperative's total locations
are limited to cultivating 100,000 square feet of Canopy. A cooperative is not limited in the
number of cultivation locations it may operate, provided that for each location over six
locations, additional application and licensing fees shall apply pursuant to {{ref:500.005(1)(d)}}. The cooperative may also conduct activities authorized for Marijuana
Product Manufacturers at up to three locations.

For the Seed-to-sale SOR, a cooperative that designates a system administrator will pay
one licensing program fee on a monthly basis for Seed-to-sale tracking software.

Members of a cooperative may not be a Person or Entity Having Direct or Indirect
Control in any other Marijuana Establishment. Such restriction may not be construed to
prohibit a Craft Marijuana Cooperative for applying for a Marijuana Retailer, Marijuana
Existing Licensee Transporter, Marijuana Research or Social Consumption Establishment
License.

Tier Expansion. A Craft Marijuana Cooperative may submit an application, in a time
and manner determined by the Commission, to change the tier in which it is classified. A
cooperative may change tiers to either expand or reduce production. If a cooperative is
applying to expand production, it shall demonstrate that while cultivating at the top of its
production tier, it has sold 85% of its product consistently over the six months preceding the
application for expanded production for an indoor cultivator, or during the harvest season
prior to the application for expanded production for an outdoor cultivator.

Tier Relegation. In connection with the license renewal process for Craft Marijuana
Cooperatives, the Commission will review the records of the cooperative during the six
months prior to the application for renewal for an indoor cultivator or during the harvest

season prior to the application for renewal for an outdoor cultivator. The Commission may
reduce the Licensee's maximum Canopy to a lower tier if the Licensee sold less than 70% of
what it produced during the six months prior to the application for renewal for an indoor
cultivator or during the harvest season prior to the application for renewal for an outdoor
cultivator.

An eligible Craft Marijuana Cooperative may operate a Supplemental On-site
Consumption license within its existing Marijuana Establishment Premises.

Marijuana Product Manufacturer. A Marijuana Product Manufacturer may obtain,
Manufacture, Process and package Marijuana Products, to transport Marijuana Products to
Marijuana Establishments and to Transfer Marijuana Products to other Marijuana
Establishments, but not to Consumers. An eligible Marijuana Product Manufacturer may operate
a Supplemental On-site Consumption license within its existing Marijuana Establishment
Premises.
Marijuana Microbusiness.
Marijuana Microbusiness.

A Microbusiness is an entity that can be either a Tier 1 Marijuana Cultivator or
Marijuana Product Manufacturer or both and, if in receipt of a Delivery Endorsement issued
by the Commission, may deliver Marijuana or Marijuana Products produced at the licensed
location directly to Consumers in compliance with established regulatory requirements for
retail sale as it relates to delivery.

A Microbusiness engaged in product manufacturing operations may purchase a
maximum of 2,000 pounds of Marijuana or its dry-weight equivalent in raw concentrate per
year from other Marijuana Establishments or MTCs.

A Microbusiness shall comply with all operational requirements imposed by {{ref:500.105}} through {{ref:500.140}} on Marijuana Cultivators and Marijuana Product Manufacturers,
and Retailers, to the extent the Licensee engages in such activities.

A Person or Entity Having Direct Control or a Person or Entity Having Indirect Control
in an existing Marijuana Establishment or MTC License that is not a Social Equity Program
Participant, Social Equity Business or Economic Empowerment Priority Applicant shall not
be eligible to apply for a Marijuana Microbusiness license. A majority of the Microbusiness'
Executives or Members shall have been residents of Massachusetts for no less than 12
months prior to application.

Delivery Endorsements shall be subject to the exclusivity provisions for Delivery
Licensees established in {{ref:500.050(10)(b)}}.

An eligible Marijuana Microbusiness may operate a Supplemental On-site Consumption
license within its existing Marijuana Establishment Premises.
Social Consumption Establishment.
Social Consumption Establishment.

A municipality may authorize the sale and on-site consumption of Marijuana and
Marijuana Products at a Social Consumption Establishment in accordance with {{extref:M.G.L.
c. 94G, § 3}}.

A Social Consumption Establishment may sell Marijuana or Marijuana Products to
Consumers and allow consumption of Marijuana or Marijuana Products by Consumers on
a Premises approved by the Commission and in a designated Consumption Area.

Social Consumption Establishments may portion servings of Marijuana and Marijuana
Products to Consumers, and White Label, Repackage, Transfer, Waste, Wholesale and
Warehouse Finished Marijuana or Marijuana Products acquired from a Marijuana
Establishment.

A Marijuana Establishment shall not allow the consumption of Marijuana or Marijuana
Products on its Premises without obtaining a Social Consumption Establishment License
from the Commission and approval of an Event Plan, if applicable.

Social Consumption Establishments shall operate all Marijuana-related activities solely
at the address identified in the license and at the address or location of the Temporary
Consumption Event Premises, if applicable.

Social Consumption Establishment Classes. A Social Consumption Establishment is
permitted to select one of the following classes:

Social Consumption Establishment Classes. A Social Consumption Establishment is
permitted to select one of the following classes:
1. Supplemental On-site Consumption.
a. A Supplemental On-site Consumption license is not granted as of right to a
Marijuana Establishment holding another license type. An eligible Marijuana
Establishment must separately apply for and obtain a Supplemental On-site
Consumption License in accordance with M.G.L c. 94G, § 3, and {{ref:500.000}}.
b.
Eligible Marijuana Retailers, Marijuana Cultivators, Marijuana Product
Manufacturers, Marijuana Delivery Operators, Microbusinesses, Craft Marijuana
Cooperatives, Third-party Transporters, or Marijuana Couriers may apply for a
Supplemental On-site Consumption License.
c. A Supplemental On-site Consumption Licensee shall be located within an
approved Marijuana Establishment's Premises that has the same Persons or Entities
Having Direct or Indirect Control.
2. Hospitality On-site Consumption.
a. Eligible applicants and eligible Marijuana Establishments may apply for a
Hospitality On-site Consumption License.
b. A Hospitality On-site Consumption Licensee or eligible applicant may be located
within a new or existing Non-Cannabis Entity.
3. Marijuana Event Organizer.
a. Eligible applicants and eligible Marijuana Establishments may apply for a
Marijuana Event Organizer License.
b. In accordance with {{ref:500.180}}, a Marijuana Event Organizer must obtain
a Host Community Agreement at its Principal Place of Business.
c. A Marijuana Event Organizer shall obtain all the necessary local permitting
required where the Temporary Consumption Event is proposed to be located prior to
the Commission's approval of an Event Plan.
d.
A Marijuana Event Organizer shall provide the Commission with all
documentation and permitting that demonstrates the Licensee obtained municipal
approval for the Temporary Consumption Event.
e. A Marijuana Event Organizer shall conduct a pre-event public safety briefing(s)
with representatives from local law enforcement, fire services, and emergency
medical services prior to any Temporary Consumption Event. The Marijuana Event
Organizer shall maintain a pre-event public safety report summarizing the topics
discussed, the date and time of the briefing(s), the names, titles and affiliations of all
participating representatives, and any recommendations, conditions, or operational
requirements issued by such representatives. The public safety briefing shall include,
at a minimum, discussion of:
1. Traffic control and parking management;
2. Crowd management and ingress and egress procedures;
3. Emergency egress routes and evacuation procedures;
4. Access for emergency responders and staging areas;
5. Communication protocols between on-site security, event staff, and first
responders; and
6. Procedures for managing public safety concerns, including but not limited to
Consumer intoxication or medical emergencies.
f. A Marijuana Event Organizer shall conduct no more than 30 single days of
permitted sales and consumption activity per municipality each calendar year.
g. A Marijuana Event Organizer shall submit a single Event Plan for a single or
multi-day Temporary Consumption Event no later than 90 days prior to the first
scheduled date of the Temporary Consumption Event. No Temporary Consumption
Event may be held without an Event Plan approved by the Commission. The Event
Plan shall include, at a minimum, the following:
1. A diagram of sufficient detail to identify the Temporary Consumption Event's
location and Premises, including designated areas for sales and service areas,
Consumption Areas, and waste, locked receptacle(s), and storage of Marijuana
and Marijuana Products, Limited Access Areas, points of entry and egress,
identification checkpoints, and the planned use of each area;

The address of the Premises or location of the Temporary Consumption
Event;
3.
A list of Marijuana Establishments, including their license numbers,
participating in the Temporary Consumption Event;
4. An attestation by the Marijuana Establishment(s) participating in the
Temporary Consumption Event which states that the entity shall comply with all
Commission regulations, and conditions, including but not limited to the
requirements set forth in {{ref:500.105(2)(b)}}8. and {{ref:500.141}};
5. A copy of the pre-event public safety report; and
6. Any other information requested by the Commission.
h. The Commission shall not approve a Licensee for participation in a Temporary
Consumption Event if the proposed participant has an active Enforcement Action,
Summary Suspension Order, or Limitation of Sales Order.

Marijuana Event Organizers are responsible for all licensed activities at a
Temporary Consumption Event, including but not limited to security, age
verification, waste, operation of consumption areas, and incident reporting.
j. Only Social Consumption Establishments, Marijuana Retailers, and Marijuana
Delivery Operators may sell Marijuana or Marijuana Products at a Temporary
Consumption Event.
k. If the list of participating Marijuana Establishments changes after the Event Plan
is submitted, or after Commission approval is issued, the Marijuana Event Organizer
shall provide notice to the Commission of the change, with an updated list of
participating Marijuana Establishments for approval by the Commission no less than
14 days prior to the Temporary Consumption Event. Failure to provide timely notice
as required shall result in the newly added Marijuana Establishment not participating
in the Temporary Consumption Event and other potential enforcement actions.
l. A Marijuana Event Organizer shall inform the Commission within 24 hours if the
Marijuana Event Organizer or a Marijuana Establishment should fail to appear at a
Temporary Consumption Event as anticipated in the Event Plan for any reason.
m. Within seven days prior to the commencement of a Temporary Consumption
Event, the Marijuana Event Organizer shall confirm with the representatives from
local law enforcement, fire services, and emergency medical services identified in
{{ref:500.050(6)(f)}}3.e., that all safety measures, operational plans, and event
logistics remain accurate and effective. If any material changes occur to the
Temporary Consumption Event, including but not limited to the layout, schedule,
staffing, capacity, security plan, or emergency response procedures, after such
confirmation, the Marijuana Event Organizer shall promptly notify the same
representatives and the Commission, and provide updated information reflecting such
changes.
n. An Event Plan shall not be approved by the Commission where there is the
planned sale or consumption of alcohol or Tobacco during the same time, and within
the same Premises.
o. A Marijuana Event Organizer Licensee shall maintain a clearly legible sign not
less than 11 inches by 17 inches in size, reading "No Persons Under 21 Allowed" at
or near each public entrance to any space or Consumption Area where the sale or
consumption of Marijuana or Marijuana Products will occur.
p. A Marijuana Event Organizer Licensee shall ensure that the sale and storage of
Marijuana or Marijuana Products is not visible from any public place or
non-age-restricted area.
q. The Commission may require a Marijuana Event Organizer and participating
Marijuana Establishments to cease operations and sales without delay if the
Commission or other governmental authorities determine it is necessary to protect the
public health and safety of Consumers or others.
r. Upon notification from the Commission or discovery by the Marijuana Event
Organizer, the Marijuana Event Organizer shall immediately expel any person selling
Marijuana or Marijuana Products without a license at the Temporary Consumption
Event. The Marijuana Event Organizer shall ensure that security is adequate to escort
the individual(s) off the Premises.
s. A Marijuana Event Organizer shall inform the Commission as soon as possible,
but no later than 24 hours if law enforcement or the municipality orders the
Temporary Consumption Event to alter operations before the planned closing of the
event.

t. A Marijuana Event Organizer shall designate a Limited Access Area(s) that can
only be accessed by the Licensee, the Licensee's Agents, participating Marijuana
Establishments and its Agents, or the Commission.
u. A Marijuana Event Organizer or participating Marijuana Establishment may
temporarily store Marijuana and Marijuana Products at a Temporary Consumption
Event for the purposes of sale to Consumers. A Marijuana Event Organizer or
participating Marijuana Establishment temporarily storing product at the Temporary
Consumption Event shall keep the Marijuana and Marijuana Products in a locked
storage compartment or container approved by the Commission. All remaining
unsold Marijuana or Marijuana Products shall be returned to its Marijuana
Establishment of origin at the end of each day of the Temporary Consumption Event.

Notwithstanding {{ref:500.110(5)}} and {{ref:500.110(6)}}, a Marijuana
Event Organizer shall not be required to install a security alarm for a Temporary
Consumption Event. Nothing in this subsection shall be construed to otherwise
exempt a Marijuana Event Organizer from compliance with security requirements set
forth in {{ref:500.110}} and {{ref:500.050(6)(f)}}3.
w. Notwithstanding {{ref:500.110(2)(b)}} and {{ref:500.110(2)(c)}}, if a
Marijuana Event Organizer submits an Alternative Security Provision for an Event
Plan, the Commission shall request that the chief municipal law enforcement officer
review the request and alternative security provision requested within ten days and
if no response is received from the chief law enforcement officer or a delegee within
10 days, the Commission shall proceed with a determination.

Violations of the requirements applicable to Temporary Consumption Events may
result in disciplinary action against the Marijuana Event Organizer and any other
Marijuana Establishment participating in the Temporary Consumption Event.
y. For sales conducted at a Temporary Consumption Event, Community Impact Fees
authorized pursuant to {{extref:M.G.L. c. 94G, § 3(d)}} and any applicable marijuana local tax
option amount due on Marijuana or Marijuana Products pursuant to {{extref:M.G.L. c. 64N}},
shall be allocated to the Host Community of the Marijuana Establishment that
conducts the sale. Community Impact Fees shall be remitted consistent with the terms
of that Host Community Agreement of the Marijuana Establishment that conducts the
sale. The Massachusetts sales tax and marijuana excise tax shall remain payable to
the Commonwealth in accordance with {{extref:M.G.L. c. 64H}} and {{extref:M.G.L. c. 64N}},
respectively.

Social Consumption Establishment licenses shall be limited on an exclusive
basis to businesses controlled by and with majority ownership comprised of
Economic Empowerment Priority Applicants or Social Equity Program Participants;
or Microbusinesses and Craft Marijuana Cooperatives, for a period of 36 months
beginning on the date on which at least one licensee in each Social Consumption
Establishment license class, Supplemental On-site Consumption, Hospitality On-site
Consumption, and Marijuana Event Organizer, has received a notice to commence
operations, provided, however, that the Commission may, by vote, decide to extend
that period following a determination that the goal of the exclusivity period to
promote and encourage full participation in the regulated Marijuana industry by
people from communities that have previously been disproportionately harmed by
Marijuana prohibition and enforcement of the law, by farmers, and by businesses of
all sizes, has not been met.
1. The Commission shall develop criteria for evaluating whether the goals of the
exclusivity period are met which shall include, but not be limited to:
a. Overall rates of participation in the regulated Marijuana industry by
people from communities that have previously been disproportionately
harmed by Marijuana prohibition and enforcement of the law, by farmers, and
by businesses of all sizes;
b. Overall rates of participation in the regulated Marijuana industry by
people of color;
c. Licenses granted to businesses with majority ownership comprised of
Economic Empowerment Priority Applicants and Social Equity Program
Participants; Microbusinesses; and Craft Marijuana Cooperatives;
d. Number of registered agents who are Social Equity Program Participants;
e. Number of Social Consumption Establishments in operation and business
performance relative to other Marijuana Establishments;

f. Financial feasibility of continued participation in the regulated Marijuana
industry by people from communities that have previously been
disproportionately harmed by Marijuana prohibition and enforcement of the
law, by farmers, and by businesses of all sizes if exclusivity period ends; and
g. Any other information the Commission determines relevant.
2. The Commission shall, in real time, collect and publicly report on data
measuring the criteria throughout the exclusivity period every 6 months. The
Commission shall begin evaluating whether the goals of the exclusivity period
have been met at least 12 months before the end of the 36-month period to
provide adequate time to consider whether an extension of the 36-month period
is necessary prior to the conclusion of that time period.
3. The licenses may be made available to any qualifying applicants after the
36-month period, unless the Commission affirmatively votes to extend the period
of exclusivity by a period of 24 months after the first 36-month period. Any
subsequent extension of the exclusivity period would require the Commission
affirmatively to find that the goals and objectives of the exclusivity period as set
forth in {{ref:500.050(6)(g)}}1., have not been met.

No person or entity other than those disclosed in the application shall be a
Person or Entity Having Direct or Indirect Control in a Social Consumption
Establishment license.

A Social Consumption Establishment is not considered to be a Marijuana
Retailer as defined under {{ref:500.002}}, but is authorized to sell Finished
Marijuana Products directly to Consumers.

A Social Consumption Establishment shall register as a vendor with the
Department of Revenue and collect and remit marijuana retail taxes in accordance
with 830 CMR 64N.1.1: Marijuana Retail Taxes.
Independent Testing Laboratory.
Independent Testing Laboratory.

Prior to final licensure an Independent Testing Laboratory shall be:
1. Accredited to the most current International Organization for Standardization (ISO)
17025 by a third-party accrediting body that is a signatory to the International Laboratory
Accreditation Cooperation (ILAC) Mutual Recognition Arrangement; or
2. Certified, registered, or accredited by an organization approved by the Commission.

An Executive or Member of a Marijuana Establishment is prohibited from being a
Person or Entity Having Direct or Indirect Control in an Independent Testing Laboratory
providing testing services for any Marijuana Establishment, except as otherwise provided in
{{ref:500.200}}.

No individual employee of a laboratory providing testing services for Marijuana
Establishments may receive direct or indirect financial compensation from any Marijuana
Establishment, except as otherwise provided in {{ref:500.200}}.

Standards Laboratory. A laboratory meeting the requirements of the Independent
Testing Laboratory may be licensed as a Standards Laboratory to ensure consistent and
compliant testing by the Independent Testing Laboratories. An Independent Testing
Laboratory may not serve as a Standards Laboratory.
1. On request by the Commission, a Standards Laboratory shall test samples of
Marijuana Products in a time and manner to be determined by the Commission.
2. Testing shall be performed in a manner determined by the Commission so as not to
reveal to the laboratory the source of the Marijuana Products.
3. The Standards Laboratory shall submit the results of testing to the Commission for
review.
4. The Standards Laboratory shall retain the Marijuana Products tested pursuant to
{{ref:500.050(7)(d)}}1., until directed to Transfer or dispose of them by the
Commission. Any disposal shall take place in compliance with {{ref:500.105(12)}}.
Marijuana Retailer.
Marijuana Retailer.
General Requirements.

General Requirements.
1. A Marijuana Retailer may purchase, transport, sell, Repackage, or otherwise Transfer
Marijuana or Marijuana Products to Marijuana Establishments and sell to Consumers.
Marijuana Retailers may sell Marijuana Accessories and Branded Goods. A Marijuana
Retailer can deliver Marijuana or Marijuana Products to Consumers in accordance with
{{ref:500.000}}. A Marijuana Retailer may not allow consumption by Consumers on
the Premises of the Marijuana Establishment unless the Marijuana Retailer obtained a
Supplemental On-site Consumption License, and the Consumption Area is approved by
the Commission.

A retailer shall operate all Marijuana-related activities solely at the address identified
in the license.
3. No Person or Entity Having Direct or Indirect Control in a Marijuana Retailer license
shall be granted or hold more than a combined total of three Marijuana Retailer Licenses
and shall be subject to the limitations in {{ref:500.050(1)(b)}}6.

A Marijuana Retailer shall provide a retail location accessible to Consumers 21 years
of age or older, or, if colocated with an MTC, Registered Qualifying Patients with the
Medical Use of Marijuana Program in possession of a Medical Registration Card.

An eligible Marijuana Retailer may operate a Supplemental On-site Consumption
license within its existing Marijuana Establishment Premises.
Marijuana Transporter.
Marijuana Transporter.

An entity may only transport Marijuana Products when such transportation is not already
authorized under a Marijuana Establishment license if it is licensed as a Marijuana
Transporter:
1.
Third-party Transporter. A Third-party Transporter is permitted to transport
Marijuana and Marijuana Products between Marijuana Establishments and between
MTCs. An eligible Third-party Transporter may operate a Supplemental On-site
Consumption license within its existing Marijuana Establishment Premises.
2. Existing Licensee Transporter. A Marijuana Establishment that wishes to contract
with other Marijuana Establishments to transport their Marijuana Products to other
Marijuana Establishments.

All Marijuana Transporter, their agents and employees, who contract with a Marijuana
Establishment to transport Marijuana Products shall comply with {{extref:M.G.L. c. 94G}}, and
{{ref:500.000}}.

Marijuana Transporters will be allowed to Warehouse Marijuana Products in a form and
manner determined by the Commission.
Marijuana Courier.
Marijuana Courier.

A Marijuana Courier may deliver Marijuana or Marijuana Products directly to
Consumers from a Marijuana Retailer or to Patients or Caregivers from an MTC with which
the Marijuana Courier has a Delivery Agreement. A Marijuana Courier may be an Owner of
or have a controlling interest in a Cultivation, Product Manufacturing, Social Consumption
Establishment, Research, Retail or Transportation license. An eligible Marijuana Courier
may operate a Supplemental On-site Consumption license within its existing Marijuana
Establishment Premises.

A Marijuana Courier shall be limited on an exclusive basis to businesses controlled by
and with majority ownership comprised of Economic Empowerment Priority Applicants or
Social Equity Program Participants for a period of 36 months from the date the first Delivery
Operator Licensee receives a notice to commence operations; provided, however, that the
Commission may vote to extend that period following a determination that the goal of the
exclusivity period to promote and encourage full participation in the regulated Marijuana
industry by people from communities that have previously been disproportionately harmed
by Marijuana prohibition and enforcement of the law has not been met; and the Commission
may vote to expand eligibility for Delivery Licenses during the exclusivity period pursuant
to {{ref:500.050(10)(b)}}4.
1. The Commission shall develop criteria for evaluating whether the goals of the
exclusivity period are met, which shall include, but not be limited to:
a. Overall rates of participation in the regulated marijuana industry by people from
communities that have previously been disproportionately harmed by marijuana
prohibition and enforcement of the law;
b. Overall rates of participation in the regulated Marijuana industry by people of
color;
c. Licenses granted to businesses with majority ownership comprised of Economic
Empowerment Priority Applicants and Social Equity Program Participants;
d. Number of registered agents who are Social Equity Program Participants;
e. Number of Delivery Licensees in operation and business performance relative to
other Marijuana Establishments;
f. Financial feasibility of continued participation in the regulated Marijuana industry
by communities that have previously been disproportionately harmed by Marijuana
prohibition and enforcement of the law if exclusivity period ends; and

g. Any other information the Commission determines relevant.
2. The Commission shall collect and report on data measuring the criteria throughout
the exclusivity period. The Commission shall begin evaluating whether the goals of the
exclusivity period have been met at least eight months before the end of the 36-month
period to provide adequate time to consider whether an extension of the 36-month period
is necessary prior to the conclusion of that time period.
3. The licenses shall generally be available to applicants after the 36-month period
unless the Commissioners affirmatively votes to extend the period of exclusivity by a
period of 12 months after the first 36-month period. Any subsequent extension of the
exclusivity period would require the Commission affirmatively to find that the goals and
objectives of the exclusivity period as set forth in {{ref:500.050(10)(f)}}1. have not
been met.
4. If data collected by the Commission demonstrates progress toward the goals and
objectives of the exclusivity period as set forth in {{ref:500.050(10)(f)}}1. and that
demand for Consumer delivery is likely to exceed the supply that could be provided by
businesses that meet the exclusivity requirements during the exclusivity period, the
Commission may vote during the exclusivity period to allow the following additional
businesses to own Delivery Licenses:
a. Worker-owned cooperatives organized to operate consistently with the Seven
Cooperative Principles established by the International Cooperative Alliance in 1995;
or
b. Massachusetts Minority Business Enterprises (MBE), Women Business
Enterprises (WBE), and Veteran Business Enterprises (VBE) with valid certification
from the SDO.
c. No person or entity other than those disclosed in the application shall be a Person
or Entity Having Direct or Indirect Control in a Delivery License.
d. No Person or Entity with Direct or Indirect Control shall possess, or be granted,
more than three Marijuana Courier Licenses.
e. After January 8, 2021, any application or license classified as a Delivery-only
license pursuant to previously adopted regulations shall be converted to a Delivery
Courier application or license governed by {{ref:500.050(10)}}.
Marijuana Delivery Operator.
Marijuana Delivery Operator.

A Delivery Operator may Wholesale and Warehouse Finished Marijuana and Finished
Marijuana Products acquired from a Marijuana Establishment, except an Independent Testing
Laboratory and deliver, sell, White Label, Repackage, or otherwise Transfer Marijuana or
Marijuana Products to Consumers. A Delivery Operator may be an Owner of or have a
controlling interest in a Cultivation, Product Manufacturing, Social Consumption
Establishment, Research, Transportation or Retail license, subject to the limitations stated
in {{ref:500.050(11)(e)}}.

A Delivery Operator Licensee shall operate a Warehouse for the purpose of storing
Finished Marijuana Products.

A Delivery Operator License does not authorize the Licensee to operate a retail
storefront.

Notwithstanding that a Delivery Operator is not considered to be a Marijuana Retailer
as defined under {{ref:500.002}} or authorized to engage in permitted activities under
{{ref:500.050(8)}}, but is authorized to sell Finished Marijuana Products directly to
consumers, a Delivery Operator shall register as a vendor with the Department of Revenue
and collect and remit marijuana retail taxes in accordance with 830 CMR 64N.1.1:
Marijuana Retail Taxes.

A Delivery Operator shall comply with the labeling and packaging requirements
contained in {{ref:500.105(5)}} and {{ref:500.105(6)}} and Requirements for Handling
of Marijuana pursuant to {{ref:500.105(3)(a)}} and (b).

Delivery Operator Licenses shall be limited on an exclusive basis to businesses controlled
by and with majority ownership comprised of Economic Empowerment Priority Applicants
or Social Equity Program Participants for a period of 36 months from the date the first
Delivery Operator Licensee receives a notice to commence operations; provided, however,
that the Commission may vote to extend that period following a determination that the goal
of the exclusivity period to promote and encourage full participation in the regulated

Marijuana industry by people from communities that have previously been disproportionately
harmed by Marijuana prohibition and enforcement of the law has not been met; and the
Commission may vote to expand eligibility for Delivery Licenses during the exclusivity
period pursuant to {{ref:500.050(11)(f)}}4.
1. The Commission shall develop criteria for evaluating whether the goals of the
exclusivity period are met, which shall include, but not be limited to:
a. Overall rates of participation in the regulated marijuana industry by people from
communities that have previously been disproportionately harmed by marijuana
prohibition and enforcement of the law;
b. Overall rates of participation in the regulated Marijuana industry by people of
color;
c. Licenses granted to businesses with majority ownership comprised of Economic
Empowerment Priority Applicants and Social Equity Program Participants;
d. Number of registered agents who are Social Equity Program Participants;
e. Number of Delivery Licensees in operation and business performance relative to
other Marijuana Establishments;
f. Financial feasibility of continued participation in the regulated Marijuana industry
by communities that have previously been disproportionately harmed by Marijuana
prohibition and enforcement of the law if exclusivity period ends; and
g. Any other information the Commission determines relevant.
2. The Commission shall collect and report on data measuring the criteria throughout
the exclusivity period. The Commission shall begin evaluating whether the goals of the
exclusivity period have been met at least eight months before the end of the 36-month
period to provide adequate time to consider whether an extension of the 36-month period
is necessary prior to the conclusion of that time period.
3. The licenses shall generally be available to applicants after the 36-month period
unless the Commissioners affirmatively votes to extend the period of exclusivity by a
period of 12 months after the first 36-month period. Any subsequent extension of the
exclusivity period would require the Commission affirmatively to find that the goals and
objectives of the exclusivity period as set forth in {{ref:500.050(11)(f)}}1. have not
been met.
4. If data collected by the Commission demonstrates progress toward the goals and
objectives of the exclusivity period as set forth in {{ref:500.050(11)(f)}}1. and that
demand for Consumer delivery is likely to exceed the supply that could be provided by
businesses that meet the exclusivity requirements during the exclusivity period, the
Commission may vote during the exclusivity period to allow the following additional
businesses to own Delivery Licenses:
a. Worker-owned cooperatives organized to operate consistently with the Seven
Cooperative Principles established by the International Cooperative Alliance in 1995;
or
b. Massachusetts Minority Business Enterprises (MBE), Women Business
Enterprises (WBE), and Veteran Business Enterprises (VBE) with valid certification
from the SDO.

No person or entity other than those disclosed in the application shall be a Person or
Entity Having Direct or Indirect Control in a Delivery Operator License.

No Person or Entity Having Direct or Indirect Control in a Delivery Operator License
shall obtain, or be granted, more than a total of three Delivery Operator Licenses.

Two years from the date the first Delivery Operator Licensee receives a notice to
commence operations, the Commission or its designee shall commence an evaluation of the
development of the Cannabis delivery market in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, which
may include assessing the competitiveness and concentration of the market, the repackaging
and white labeling requirements, and any other matter as determined by the Commission. The
Commission shall complete its evaluation within four months, unless the Commission
determines that there is a reasonable basis for an extension. The Commission may take any
action including, but not limited to, issuing regulations or guidance, it deems necessary to
address issues with market development.

An eligible Delivery Operator may operate a Supplemental On-site Consumption License
within its existing Marijuana Establishment Premises.
Marijuana Research Facility Licensee.
Marijuana Research Facility Licensee.

A Marijuana Research Facility Licensee may conduct research after receiving approval
from the Commission. A license to operate a Marijuana Research Facility shall be separate
from receipt of a Research Permit to conduct a specific research project at the Marijuana
Research Facility.

A Marijuana Research Facility Licensee may be an academic institution, nonprofit
corporation or domestic corporation or entity authorized to do business in the
Commonwealth, including a licensed Marijuana Establishment or MTC.

Unless otherwise authorized by law, any Marijuana Research Facility Licensee that is
not licensed pursuant to {{ref:500.050}} or 935 CMR 501.050: Medical Marijuana
Treatment Centers (MTCs) to engage in the cultivation, production or retail sale of Marijuana
or Marijuana Products shall acquire all Marijuana or Marijuana Products used in research
from a Marijuana Establishment or MTC licensed to engage in such activity except:
1. A Marijuana Research Facility Licensee may engage in cultivation or product
manufacturing of Marijuana or Marijuana Products if the cultivation or product
manufacturing process is the subject of its research; or
2. As otherwise determined by the Commission.

A Marijuana Research Facility may be colocated with another Marijuana Establishment
or MTC license provided that the Marijuana Research Facility and the colocated licensed
Marijuana Establishment or MTC are:
1. Commonly owned; and
2. Clearly physically separated.

A Marijuana Research Facility Licensee may not Transfer Marijuana or Marijuana
Products to another Marijuana Establishment, other than for testing, or sell to a Consumer,
Registered Qualifying Patient or Caregiver Marijuana or Marijuana Products that has been
acquired for a research project under its Marijuana Research Facility License.
